new_destinations.span_note: Spots run from Cahills Crossing/Ubirr in the north to Gunlom and Maguk in the south (about 115 km north-south) and Injalak at Gunbalanya in the east; 150 km keeps all within 75% of the span once the centre sits near the middle of the park (about Cooinda-Jabiru).

new_destinations.reason: Flagship park (3 counted sources, 48,810 views); its villages, walks, falls and rock art are its spots.

new_destinations.name: Arnhem Land
new_destinations.coordinates_source: none usable: candidate gave the Wikipedia region centroid (-12.73,134.59), which is the middle of the whole region and not where visitors go. The destination is centred on the Gove Peninsula (the middle of Nhulunbuy, Yirrkala and the beaches) via resolve-pin; it must differ from the Nhulunbuy spot pin
new_destinations.span_note: Spots: Nhulunbuy, Yirrkala (19 km), Cape Wirrawoi (5 km), East Woody Beach/Island, Macassan Beach (about 35 minutes), Rainbow Cliffs, Bremer Island offshore. 100 km covers them; recheck once pins are resolved.
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage region page "Arnhem Land" (lists Nhulunbuy, Yirrkala and the Gove beaches); Tourism NT region "Arnhem Land" (northernterritory.com/us/en/arnhem-land, with the Nhulunbuy (Gove) destination page and bucket list). Region name preferred over the town Nhulunbuy because the draws are the beaches, island and Yirrkala around it. Alternative name for the owner: "Nhulunbuy & Gove Peninsula". Note: the vast Aboriginal-owned Arnhem Land beyond Gove is permit-only; Gunbalanya (Injalak Arts) sits in the west and is placed under Kakadu because Kakadu tours reach it, and Garig Gunak Barlu is about 500 km west and stands alone.
new_destinations.reason: The kept candidate "Arnhem Land" (86,682 views, 2 counted sources) is the destination itself; 8 kept spots cluster on the Gove Peninsula.
